Step–1  Degree of unsaturation required by the spectra  
• Benzene ring = 4 double-bond equivalents (DBE).  
• Ester carbonyl = +1 DBE.  
• An alkene (two vinylic protons are observed) = +1 DBE.  
Total DBE seen in the spectra = 6.

Step–2  DBE supplied by the four candidate formulae  
A. C₁₂H₁₂O₂ DBE = 12 – 12/2 + 1 = 7  
B. C₁₁H₁₄O₂ DBE = 11 – 14/2 + 1 = 5  
C. C₁₁H₁₂O₂ DBE = 11 – 12/2 + 1 = 6  
D. C₁₂H₁₄O₂ DBE = 12 – 14/2 + 1 = 6

Only C and D supply the required 6 DBE.

Step–3  Number and kinds of hydrogens implied by the ¹H NMR  
• 2 equivalent aromatic proton sets → 4 aromatic H  
• 2 vinylic H (doublet and doublet of quartets) → 2 H  
• 2 methyl groups (3 H each) → 6 H  
Total H accounted for by the spectrum = 4 + 2 + 6 = 12 H.

Step–4  Compare with candidate formulae  
• C₁₁H₁₂O₂ contains exactly the 12 hydrogens seen.  
• C₁₂H₁₄O₂ contains 14 hydrogens – two hydrogens more than are present in the NMR; no signals for an extra CH₂, OH, or additional CH₃ are reported.

Therefore the only formula fully consistent with both the degree of unsaturation and the number and types of hydrogens observed is C₁₁H₁₂O₂.

Answer: C
